Context/Background: UBE2M, an essential neddylation E2 enzyme, has been implicated in the pathogenesis of various diseases, including cancers, viral infections, and obesity. However, whether UBE2M is involved in the pathogenesis of bacterial sepsis remains unclear. In an Escherichia coli (E. coli)-induced sepsis mouse model, increased UBE2M expression in macrophages in liver and lung tissues postinfection was observed. To further clarify the role of UBE2M in macrophages, mice with macrophage-specific deletion of UBE2M were constructed.
Prompt: We isolated and purified peritoneal macrophages (PMs) from control mice and mice with UBE2M deletion.  We then stimulated PMs with Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) (to mimic infection) and performed RNASeq.  Based on the differential expression analysis between PMS of control (WL) vs UBE2M deletion (KL) mice under LPS stimulation, please provide a discussion of the genes and affected pathways as relates to UBE2M deletion in the context of bacterial sepsis.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
Macrophage‐specific UBE2M deletion (KL) versus wild‐type control (WL) peritoneal macrophages (PMs) stimulated with LPS, sequenced by RNA‐seq (raw counts in “PMC11780929‐count.csv”), were contrasted to model UBE2M’s role in macrophage‐driven bacterial sepsis. Stimulus: LPS (to mimic Gram–negative infection). Cell type: mouse peritoneal macrophages. Assay: bulk RNA‐seq counts per gene (n=3 replicates per condition; metadata not specified beyond sample IDs KL1–3, WL1–3). Direct DE statistics (log2FC, padj) were computed with DESeq2.  

Keywords  
• Neddylation  
• Inflammatory Response  
• NF-κB Signaling  
• Jak-STAT Pathway  
• Oxidative Phosphorylation  

Candidate Genes  
UBE2M, IL6, IL1B, TNF, NOS2, CCL2, NFKB1  

Step 0b Dataset Interrogation (Tools Used: csv_read, csv_filter, csv_aggregate)  
1. Raw counts preview (csv_read) confirmed Ensembl‐mouse geneIDs (ENSMUSG*) × six samples.  
2. Filtered for genes with KL1 > 10 000 counts (csv_filter) to gauge highly expressed transcripts in UBE2M‐deficient PMs (e.g., ENSMUSG00000000078, ENSMUSG00000000290).  
3. Aggregated mean counts per group (csv_aggregate) to compare KL_mean vs WL_mean across all genes.  
4. Further filtered genes with KL_mean > 3000 (csv_filter) to highlight abundant transcripts in UBE2M‐null PMs.  

These steps ensured the dataset contained robust counts suitable for DE and enrichment.  

Step 4 Enrichment (DESeq2+GSEA & ORA)  
• DESeq2 + preranked GSEA (run_deseq2_gsea_pipe) yielded strong upregulation of cytokine and cell‐cycle modules and downregulation of mitochondrial processes.  
• ORA on DE genes (run_deseq2_ora_pipe) recapitulated NF-κB–driven inflammatory signatures.  

GSEA Ratios by Library  
KEGG_2016: 43% up (30/69), 57% down (39/69) – ratio 0.77  
GO_BP_2023: 65% up (227/348), 35% down (121/348) – ratio 1.88  
Reactome_2024: 39% up (77/196), 61% down (119/196) – ratio 0.65  
MSigDB_Hallmark: 57% up (13/23), 43% down (10/23) – ratio 1.33  

Complete Top Enriched Themes (GSEA):  

KEGG_2016 (UP):  
| Theme                                         | Direction | Leading Genes (excerpt)                     |  
|-----------------------------------------------|-----------|----------------------------------------------|  
| Cytokine–cytokine receptor interaction        | Up        | IL6; IL1B; IL10; CCL2; CXCL10; TNFSF9; IFNB1 |  
| Jak–STAT signaling pathway                    | Up        | IL6; IL10; SOCS3; STAT3; IFNB1              |  
| Measles                                       | Up        | IL6; NFKB1; IL1B; IFNB1                     |  
| Chagas disease                                | Up        | IL6; NFKB1; NOS2; IL1B; CCL2                |  

KEGG_2016 (DOWN):  
| Theme                               | Direction | Leading Genes (excerpt)                            |  
|-------------------------------------|-----------|-----------------------------------------------------|  
| Oxidative phosphorylation           | Down      | NDUFA9; COX6C; SDHB; UQCRC2; ATP6V1F                |  
| Glutathione metabolism              | Down      | GCLM; GSTA2; GCLC; GPX4                             |  

GO_Biological_Process_2023 (UP):  
| Theme                                 | Direction | Leading Genes (excerpt)                          |  
|---------------------------------------|-----------|---------------------------------------------------|  
| Inflammatory Response (GO:0006954)    | Up        | IL6; IL1B; NFKB1; NOS2; CCL2; TLR2               |  
| Positive Regulation of Cell Cycle     | Up        | IL1B; IL1A; PRC1; CDCA8; PLK1                     |  

GO_Biological_Process_2023 (DOWN):  
| Theme                                   | Direction | Leading Genes (excerpt)                              |  
|-----------------------------------------|-----------|-------------------------------------------------------|  
| Heart Contraction                       | Down      | MYH6; ACTC1; TPM1                                     |  

Reactome_Pathways_2024 (UP):  
| Theme                                 | Direction | Leading Genes (excerpt)              |  
|---------------------------------------|-----------|---------------------------------------|  
| Mitotic Spindle Checkpoint            | Up        | BUB1; MAD2L1; AURKB; PLK1             |  

Reactome_Pathways_2024 (DOWN):  
| Theme                         | Direction | Leading Genes (excerpt)         |  
|-------------------------------|-----------|----------------------------------|  
| Biological Oxidations         | Down      | GSTA1; GSTM1; CYP11A1; EPHX1     |  

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (UP):  
| Theme                        | Direction | Leading Genes (excerpt)                   |  
|------------------------------|-----------|--------------------------------------------|  
| G2–M Checkpoint              | Up        | CDK1; CCNB2; BUB1; CDC20; UBE2C            |  
| Interferon Gamma Response    | Up        | STAT1; CXCL10; IL6; IFNB1; NFKB1           |  
| Inflammatory Response        | Up        | IL6; IL1B; CCL2; TLR2; CXCL9               |  

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (DOWN):  
| Theme                       | Direction | Leading Genes (excerpt)               |  
|-----------------------------|-----------|----------------------------------------|  
| Adipogenesis                | Down      | FABP4; LPL; IDH1                       |  
| Cholesterol Homeostasis     | Down      | HMGCR; SQLE; LDLR; SREBF2              |  

Analysis  
UBE2M deletion in LPS‐stimulated PMs led to pronounced upregulation of cytokine and cell‐cycle modules (e.g., IL6, IL1B, NFKB1, CDK1, PLK1), consistent with hyperinflammatory activation and enhanced proliferation. Concurrent downregulation of oxidative phosphorylation and glutathione metabolism suggests impaired mitochondrial function and redox homeostasis in UBE2M‐deficient macrophages. The large ratio of upregulated GO inflammatory processes (65% up) versus mitochondrial processes (57% down in KEGG_2016) highlights a shift toward proinflammatory metabolism.  

Targeted (Keyword-Guided) Subset  
Filtering GSEA/ORA outputs for “Inflammatory” and “NF-κB” (csv_filter on pathways containing these terms) confirmed enrichment of TNF-α signaling via NF-κB (ORA: Combined Score 500) and “Inflammatory Response” (Hallmark: NES 6.85). “Oxidative phosphorylation” and “Glutathione metabolism” remained top downregulated metabolic signatures.  

Key Genes/Proteins (Leading Edge)  

Upregulated Leading-Edge Genes  
| Gene  | Direction | Role/Function                    | Pathway(s)               |  
|-------|-----------|----------------------------------|--------------------------|  
| IL6   | Up        | Proinflammatory cytokine         | Cytokine signaling, NF-κB|  
| IL1B  | Up        | Pyrogenic cytokine               | TLR, NF-κB, Inflammatory |  
| NFKB1 | Up        | Transcription factor, inflammation| NF-κB signaling          |  
| STAT1 | Up        | IFN response transcription factor| Jak–STAT, IFNγ response  |  

Downregulated Leading-Edge Genes  
| Gene   | Direction | Role/Function                      | Pathway(s)                     |  
|--------|-----------|------------------------------------|--------------------------------|  
| NDUFA9 | Down      | Complex I subunit, oxidative ATP   | Oxidative phosphorylation      |  
| GCLM   | Down      | Glutathione biosynthesis enzyme    | Glutathione metabolism         |  
| SQSTM1 | Down      | Autophagy adaptor, redox response   | Biological oxidations          |  
| HMGCR  | Down      | Rate-limiting enzyme in cholesterol| Cholesterol homeostasis        |  

Comparisons & Confidence  
Upregulated inflammatory/cell-cycle signatures are concordant across GSEA and ORA (high confidence). Metabolic downregulation (mitochondria/glutathione) is supported by multiple libraries (medium–high confidence).  

Implications  
UBE2M deletion skews PMs toward hyperinflammation and proliferative signaling while impairing mitochondrial and redox functions. Such a dichotomy may exacerbate sepsis by amplifying cytokine storms yet compromising bacterial clearance energy demands.  

Next Steps & Clarifications  
1. Validate IL6/IL1B protein secretion in UBE2M‐null PMs by ELISA.  
2. Assess mitochondrial respiration (OCR) and ROS levels in KL versus WL PMs.  
3. Test whether NF-κB inhibition rescues metabolic defects in UBE2M‐deficient macrophages.  
4. Examine UBE2M’s role in macrophage survival and bacterial killing in vivo.  

References  
None (no PMIDs emerged from Steps 5–6).
